# Vertical overlay: Critical Manufacturing

**Level:** CISA critical infrastructure sector (child of NAICS 31-33 Manufacturing)
**Primary industry for Cris Santos Company:** NAICS 335311 Power, Distribution, and Specialty Transformer Manufacturing. Power and distribution transformer manufacturer.
**Primary system:** ERP and production scheduling system

## Regulators and sector risk management agency
SRMA: Department of Homeland Security (CISA); Department of Commerce BIS (EAR; ICTS connected-vehicle rule); Department of Defense (for defense supply chain)

## Primary regulation for the gap analysis (P03)
**NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 with NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (OT)**, NIST CSWP 29 (Feb. 26, 2024); NIST SP 800-82r3 (Sep. 2023). No binding sector-wide cyber regulation exists for critical manufacturing; CSF 2.0 + SP 800-82r3 is the federal reference baseline for IT/OT. Where the manufacturer is a DoD supplier, substitute NIST SP 800-171 R2 / CMMC Level 2 as the binding target.
Source: https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/cswp/29/the-nist-cybersecurity-framework-csf-20/final

## Sector context
- **Sensitive data:** Product designs / trade secrets; EAR-controlled technology; CUI (defense suppliers); Vehicle and telematics data; Supplier/BOM data
- **Critical systems:** PLCs, robotics and CNC; MES and SCADA; PLM/CAD; ERP and supply-chain planning; Industrial IoT/historians; Vehicle telematics/OTA update infrastructure
- **Sector AI rules and guidance:** None identified beyond cross-sector obligations
- **Assurance alternatives to SOC 2:** None noted
- **Scenario incident (P08):** Ransomware disrupting production of grid equipment
- **Scenario AI use case (P10):** Demand forecasting and predictive maintenance

## Notes
Critical manufacturing is one of the explicit CIRCIA sector criteria, so once final, most NAICS 331/333/335/336 manufacturers would be covered regardless of size.
